chainNotes.title: Robinhood Chain publishes no L2 sequencer-uptime feed, yet its docs require checking one
chainNotes.statement: Robinhood's oracle documentation instructs callers to "verify the sequencer is up before trusting a price" because during a sequencer outage feeds can go stale. No such feed could be found: the Robinhood Chain Chainlink reference-data directory contains 58 feeds and none is a sequencer-uptime feed, and chain 4663 does not appear on Chainlink's L2 Sequencer Uptime Feeds page, which lists Arbitrum, Base, Celo, Mantle, MegaETH, Metis, OP, Scroll, Soneium, X Layer and ZKsync. The recommended control therefore cannot be performed on this chain today. Stated as "not found in the published directories" rather than "does not exist".

chainNotes.title: 160 of 195 scanned Stock Tokens have no Chainlink price feed
chainNotes.statement: The Robinhood Chain Chainlink reference-data directory publishes 58 feeds, of which 35 are 24/5 equity feeds. 160 of the 195 Stock Tokens scanned have no feed entry, so they cannot be priced on-chain at all and any valuation must come from an off-chain source — which reintroduces the cross-surface mixing hazard. 23 of them also carry a uiMultiplier() other than 1.0, where an off-chain SHARE price differs from token value by that multiplier: CRM (1.0011x), CRWD (4.0000x), AVGO (1.0013x), CCL (1.0215x), PR (1.0045x), and 18 more.

findings.subject: CRM (0xd95B44124e475743a7589e68F3D74008A5536D44)
findings.affectedParty: Any integrator that presents CRM balanceOf() as a share count. The contract itself is behaving as ERC-8056 specifies and is not at fault.
findings.title: CRM: reading balanceOf() as shares understates by 0.1147% (multiplier 1.001148323x)
findings.statement: CRM reports uiMultiplier() = 1001148322800714293 (1.001148323), which is CORRECT AND SPEC-COMPLIANT behaviour under ERC-8056 — this finding is not a defect in the token contract. It records the exposure carried by a caller that reads balanceOf() as shares. Under ERC-8056 a corporate action moves the multiplier rather than balances, so balanceOf() returns tokens and share-equivalents = balance * uiMultiplier() / 1e18. A surface presenting the raw balance as a share count understates it by 0.1147% (the true count is 1.0011x the raw balance). Token value computed as balance * Chainlink feed price is unaffected, because the feed is already multiplier-adjusted.

impact.measures: how far a raw balanceOf() read as shares understates the true share count, as a share of the true count
impact.note: totalSupply raw 267.4830 tokens vs 267.7901 share-equivalents (delta 0.3071). Presenting the raw balance as a share count understates by 0.1147%; equivalently the true count is 1.0011x the raw.

findings.subject: SPY (0x117cc2133c37B721F49dE2A7a74833232B3B4C0C)
findings.affectedParty: Any caller that values SPY with an off-chain SHARE price, or computes a premium/discount between the on-chain token price and an off-chain share price.
findings.title: SPY: off-chain share price and on-chain token price differ by 0.172%
findings.statement: The Chainlink feed returns a multiplier-adjusted TOKEN price (770.5816), while Robinhood's REST /prices endpoint returns the RAW UNDERLYING share price (mid 767.6350). These are different quantities related by uiMultiplier(): underlying x 1.001717991 = 768.9538, leaving a residual of 0.212% against the observed feed price. That residual is NOT small relative to the 0.172% multiplier effect, so it is reported as an observation and no cause is asserted for it. Bid/ask spread and quote timing are plausible contributors but are not established here; a trading halt on the underlying would also produce it, and this sweep does not test that. The finding stands on the multiplier relationship itself, which is byte-verified: valuing balanceOf() with an off-chain share price, or computing a premium/discount between an on-chain token price and an off-chain share price, produces a phantom error of 0.172%.

impact.measures: how far the on-chain token price differs from the off-chain share price, as a share of the share price
impact.note: feed 770.5816 vs underlying-mid 767.6350 x multiplier 1.001717991 = 768.9538

offChainSources.describes: underlying share bid/ask used for the mid 767.6350 (not multiplier-adjusted)

That residual is NOT small relative to the 0.057% multiplier effect, so it is reported as an observation and no cause is asserted for it. Bid/ask spread and quote timing are plausible contributors but are not established here; a trading halt on the underlying would also produce it, and this sweep does not test that. The finding stands on the multiplier relationship itself, which is byte-verified: valuing balanceOf() with an off-chain share price, or computing a premium/discount between an on-chain token price and an off-chain share price, produces a phantom error of 0.057%.

impact.measures: how far the on-chain token price differs from the off-chain share price, as a share of the share price

findings.subject: HPE (0x59dd09d4900C2E4B5F75b7c0d4E6796fcc234Cb1)
findings.affectedParty: Any integrator that presents HPE balanceOf() as a share count. The contract itself is behaving as ERC-8056 specifies and is not at fault.
findings.title: HPE: reading balanceOf() as shares understates by 0.1714% (multiplier 1.001716958x)
findings.statement: HPE reports uiMultiplier() = 1001716957939304938 (1.001716958), which is CORRECT AND SPEC-COMPLIANT behaviour under ERC-8056 — this finding is not a defect in the token contract. It records the exposure carried by a caller that reads balanceOf() as shares. Under ERC-8056 a corporate action moves the multiplier rather than balances, so balanceOf() returns tokens and share-equivalents = balance * uiMultiplier() / 1e18. A surface presenting the raw balance as a share count understates it by 0.1714% (the true count is 1.0017x the raw balance). Token value computed as balance * Chainlink feed price is unaffected, because the feed is already multiplier-adjusted.
